title: Friends
hookLine: friendship is a school of love
tomorrow: who prays for the people throwing the stones?

cards: A teammate passes you the ball. A friend notices you haven't touched it all game, and asks why on the ride home. So what's the difference between a friend and a teammate?
Jesus draws that line himself, the night before he dies, in John's Gospel. He tells his disciples he won't call them servants anymore, because a servant doesn't know what his master is doing.
Then, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: "But I have called you friends."

teach.b: His reason is the surprise: friends, because everything he heard from his Father he has made known to them. A servant gets a task.
A friend gets told what's going on inside. That's the line. Teammates share a goal; friends share what's real.
And notice when he says it: not at a celebration, but at supper, hours before his arrest. He tells them they're friends right before the long night. Friendship isn't only for the good seasons.
It's what holds when things go dark.

teach.h: YOU AND I, AND A THIRD.
teach.b: A Cistercian abbot named Aelred of Rievaulx wrote a whole dialogue on spiritual friendship, and he opens it with a picture: here we are, you and I, and I hope a third, Christ, in the middle of us.
That's why the tradition calls friendship a school of love. Look back at this week.
Every lesson gets practiced on a friend first: full attention, choosing again after you let someone down, telling the truth kindly, running toward someone after a fight.
Friends are where you rehearse it, and where you get it wrong safely enough to try again.

how: Catholics hear Jesus's words about friendship from John 15 at Mass, and some still read Aelred of Rievaulx's Spiritual Friendship, alone or with a friend.

o: anyone who shares your goals or your team
the ones you tell what's real, where love is practiced
the people you see the most in a normal week

games.q: this week's people — tap the pairs.

s: in John's Gospel, Jesus calls his disciples friends instead of servants
because he made known to them everything he heard from his Father.
in Mark, Jesus loved the rich man only after he agreed to follow
the look and the love came first; the man walked away sad.
honoring parents means agreeing with them
at twelve, Jesus told them the honest thing and still went home with them.

games.q: a girl from practice only texts you when she needs a ride. you actually like her. going by John 15, what turns a teammate into a friend?
o: keep giving rides; showing up is all friendship is.
tell her something real about your week, and ask about hers.
stop the rides until she proves she's a real friend.
games.why: in John, the line between servant and friend is being told what's real. rides are kind; sharing what's inside is what makes a friend.

practice: Count your friends on your fingers, slowly: the ones who know what's going on inside you, now or once. Give each finger a name and a second of thanks.
When you reach the last one, pick one name you'd like to spend real time with soon, and start to plan it.

wordCard.voice: Friends. The ones you tell what's real, where love gets practiced first. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek, John's Gospel: friends, the word Jesus uses instead of servants.

carryVoice: Your line: a school of love. Jesus called them friends because he told them everything. One week of people, done.
